item.text:
# Félix Tshisekedi in 2024: 2B.2 research note

## Bottom line
I found **no credible evidence** that Tshisekedi initiated a war of choice, annexation campaign, or overt cross-border coercion in 2024. The record is mostly a **defensive eastern-DRC conflict** plus repeated diplomacy.

The main counterpoint is that he still leaned on **military buildup** and **proxy militias** in a way that could prolong and widen the conflict beyond strict defensive necessity. So the best reading is:

- **No clear war-of-choice / annexation evidence**
- **Yes, some proxy-conflict and militarized escalation beyond a purely defensive posture**

## Evidence against 2B.2

- [Crise sécuritaire dans l’Est de la Rdc : Les Présidents Félix Tshisekedi et Salva Kiir appellent au respect des accords de paix](https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/crise_securitaire_dans_lest_de_la_rdc_les_presidents_felix_tshisekedi_et_salva_kiir_appellent_au_respect_des_accords_de_paix)  
  - **Publisher:** Présidence RDC  
  - **Date:** 2024-03-25  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Tshisekedi publicly called for an urgent relaunch of the Nairobi and Luanda peace processes and said he would spare no effort to restore peace, security, and stability in eastern Congo and the region. This is direct evidence against a war-of-choice reading.  
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 1B.4, 1B.8

- [Crise sécuritaire dans l’Est de la RDC : Les Présidents Félix Tshisekedi Et Joao Lourenco appellent au respect du cessez-le-feu](https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/crise_securitaire_dans_lest_de_la_rdc_les_presidents_felix_tshisekedi_et_joao_lourenco_appellent_au_respect_du_cessez_le_feu)  
  - **Publisher:** Présidence RDC  
  - **Date:** 2024-08-12  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Tshisekedi backed the Luanda process, welcomed the 4 August ceasefire, and said his government was available for the next negotiation steps. That is strong evidence that he was still choosing diplomacy when a peaceful path existed.  
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 1B.4, 1B.8

- [Readout of the Secretary-General’s meeting with H.E. Mr. Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://www.un.org/sg/en/content/sg/readouts/2024-09-24/readout-of-the-secretary-generals-meeting-he-mr-felix-antoine-tshisekedi-tshilombo-president-of-the-democratic-republic-of-the-congo-scroll-down-for-french)  
  - **Publisher:** UN Secretary-General  
  - **Date:** 2024-09-24  
  - **Claim-level summary:** The UN said Tshisekedi discussed eastern DRC and ongoing regional peace efforts with the Secretary-General. This supports a continued diplomacy-first approach rather than a cross-border coercion strategy.  
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 1B.4, 1B.8

- [Congo and Rwanda say peace talks in Angola will not take place](https://yahoo.com/news/congo-rwanda-peace-talks-angola-130008004.html)  
  - **Publisher:** Reuters  
  - **Date:** 2024-12-15  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported that the planned Angola summit collapsed, with the DRC presidency saying the Rwandan delegation refused to participate. This shows Tshisekedi was still operating through diplomatic channels rather than trying to impose a military solution.  
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 1B.4, 1B.8

## Evidence cutting against 2B.2

- [Face à la presse, le Président Félix Tshisekedi a peint un tableau d’espoir de la RDC](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/face_a_la_presse_le_president_felix_tshisekedi_a_peint_un_tableau_despoir_de_la_rdc)  
  - **Publisher:** Présidence RDC  
  - **Date:** 2024-02-23  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Tshisekedi emphasized a major military buildup and a force-forward approach to the eastern security problem, while still saying he wanted lasting peace. This is the clearest evidence that force was not merely a last resort.  
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 1B.3, 1B.7

- [Army disarray hobbles Congo's fight with Rwanda-backed rebels, officers say](https://theprint.in/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/2160048/)  
  - **Publisher:** Reuters  
  - **Date:** 2024-07-17  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported that the government relied on a loose alliance of pro-government militias known as Wazalendo, that the army had no control over them, and that they were often poorly trained and undisciplined. Tshisekedi reportedly instructed that Wazalendo be brought in line, but the dependence on proxies is the key negative signal here.  
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 1B.6, 1B.7, 1B.3

- [Around 20 civilians killed in Congo attack, army and M23 trade blame](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/around-20-civilians-killed-in-congo-attack-army-and-m23-trade-blame-3283402)  
  - **Publisher:** Reuters  
  - **Date:** 2024-01-25  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters described the fighting as an offensive by Congolese troops and M23 rebels in a long-running conflict that had already caused major displacement. This is not proof of a war of choice, but it is evidence that Tshisekedi was presiding over a kinetic campaign rather than a pure defensive posture.  
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 1B.1, 1B.4

## Search gap

- I found **no credible evidence** that Tshisekedi sought annexation, covert destabilization, or deliberate cross-border aggression in 2024.
- I also found **no reliable evidence** of a proactive offensive war initiated for expansion or domestic diversion.
- The strongest negative evidence is **proxy reliance** and **military-first rhetoric**, not an actual war of choice. So the record is **more defensive than aggressive**, but not cleanly restraint-only.
